'''Boris Semyonovich Tsirelson''' ({{langx|he|בוריס סמיונוביץ' צירלסון}}, {{langx|ru|Борис Семёнович Цирельсон}}; May 4, 1950 – January 21, 2020) was a Russian–Israeli mathematician and Professor of Mathematics at [[Tel Aviv University]] in Israel, as well as a [[Wikipedian|Wikipedia editor]].

==Biography==
[[File:BorisTsirelsonStudent.jpg|thumb|upright=0.7|Tsirelson while a first-year student, in 1967]]

Tsirelson was born in [[Saint Petersburg|Leningrad]] to a [[History of the Jews in Russia|Russian Jewish]] family. From his father Simeon's side, he was the great-nephew of rabbi [[Yehuda Leib Tsirelson]], chief rabbi of [[Bessarabia]] from 1918 to 1941, and a prominent [[posek]] and Jewish leader. He obtained his Master of Science from the [[Saint Petersburg State University|University of Leningrad]] and remained there to pursue graduate studies. He obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in 1975, with thesis "General properties of bounded Gaussian processes and related questions" written under the direction of [[Ildar Abdulovich Ibragimov]].<ref name="MG"/>

Later, he participated in the [[Refusenik (Soviet Union)|refusenik]] movement, but only received permission to immigrate to Israel in 1991. From then until 2017, he was a professor at [[Tel-Aviv University]].

He also worked on fault-tolerant [[cellular automaton]].<ref>{{Citation |last=Cirel'son |first=B. S. |chapter=Reliable storage of information in a system of unreliable components with local interactions |date=1978 |title=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |pages=15–30 |chapter-url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1007/bfb0070081 |access-date=2024-11-14 |place=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg |isbn=978-3-540-08450-1}}</ref>

In 1998 he was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Tsirelson, Boris|chapter=Within and beyond the reach of Brownian innovation|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. III|year=1998|pages=311–320|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011588000}}</ref>

==Contributions to mathematics==
Tsirelson made notable contributions to [[probability theory]] and [[functional analysis]]. These include:

* [[Tsirelson's bound]], in [[quantum mechanics]], is an inequality, related to the issue of [[quantum nonlocality]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Wehner|first=Stephanie|date=2006-02-14|title=Tsirelson bounds for generalized Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt inequalities|journal=[[Physical Review A]]|volume=73|issue=2|article-number=022110|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.73.022110|arxiv=quant-ph/0510076|bibcode=2006PhRvA..73b2110W|s2cid=118979741 }}</ref>
* [[Tsirelson space]] is an example of a [[reflexive space|reflexive]] [[Banach space]] in which neither a [[lp space|''l<sup>&nbsp;p</sup>'' space]] nor a [[lp space|''c''<sub>0</sub> space]] can be embedded.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Mujica|first=J.|date=2001-04-01|title=Ideals of holomorphic functions on Tsirelson's space|journal=Archiv der Mathematik|language=en|volume=76|issue=4|pages=292–298|doi=10.1007/s000130050571|s2cid=121557408 |issn=0003-889X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Maurey|first=Bernard|date=1995-01-01|publisher=Birkhäuser Basel|isbn=978-3-0348-9902-4|editor-last=Lindenstrauss|editor-first=J.|series=Operator Theory Advances and Applications|pages=131–142|language=en|editor-last2=Milman|editor-first2=V.|editor2-link=Vitali D. Milman|doi=10.1007/978-3-0348-9090-8_13|title = Geometric Aspects of Functional Analysis|chapter = A Remark about Distortion|arxiv = math/9306212|s2cid=118086685 }}</ref>
* The [[Tsirelson's stochastic differential equation|Tsirelson's drift]], a counterexample in the theory of [[stochastic differential equations]], is an SDE which has a weak solution but no strong solution. 
* The [[Gaussian isoperimetric inequality]] (proved by [[Vladimir Sudakov]] and Tsirelson, and independently by [[Christer Borell]]), stating that [[affine halfspace]]s are the isoperimetric sets for the [[Probability space|Gaussian measure]].

== Death ==
Tsirelson died on January 21, 2020, at the age of 69.<ref>{{cite web |date=2020-02-25 |title=The School of Mathematical Sciences mourns the death of our colleague, Professor Boris Tsirelson |url=https://en-exact-sciences.tau.ac.il/math/Tsirelsonborisen |archive-url=https://archive.today/20200226133746/https://en-exact-sciences.tau.ac.il/math/Tsirelsonborisen  |archive-date=February 26, 2020 |access-date=2026-06-23 |website=School of Mathematical Sciences}}</ref>
